title: GatorPlate Brain API v1
description: Contract between GatorPlate's brain and its two clients: the hosted voice gateway (phone, English) and the GatorPlate talk page (web, English and Spanish). The gateway handles audio and timing; GatorPlate decides every word. Requests carry text, events and counters only: never audio, never the student's phone number or anything derived from it. Frozen 2026-10-01. Human reference: docs/BRAIN_API.md. Test vectors: contracts/examples/. Checker: contracts/check_examples.py.

x-version.change_policy: Request fields may be added inside v1 (receivers ignore unknown request fields). Reply fields, enum values, error codes, auth and endpoint meanings change only with a new version (/v2 paths and "v": 2).

x-auth.call_id_source: phone: the gateway creates a new random UUID (version 4) for every call and writes it as 32 lowercase hex characters without dashes; web: issued by POST /api/web/sessions

gateway.timestamp_format: unix seconds as a decimal integer string (digits only)

signing_string_parts.ts: the X-GP-Timestamp header value exactly as sent
signing_string_parts.METHOD: HTTP method in upper case: GET or POST
signing_string_parts.path: URL path exactly as sent, without scheme, host or query string (GET /v1/lines?lang=en signs /v1/lines)
signing_string_parts.sha256_hex(body): lowercase hex SHA-256 of the exact body bytes sent; for an empty body (GET) e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855

gateway.signature_format: v1=<lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256(key, signing_string as UTF-8)>
gateway.key: UTF-8 bytes of the shared secret string exactly as stored (do not base64-decode it)
gateway.secret_format: 48 random bytes as URL-safe base64 text
check_order: X-GP-Timestamp or X-GP-Signature missing (and no bearer token): 401 unauthorized
timestamp not digits, or signature not 'v1=' + 64 lowercase hex: 401 bad_signature
channel in a start body is not phone: 401 unauthorized

web.bound_to: the call_id issued together with the token
web.errors: missing, unknown or expired token, token issued for another call_id, or a start body whose channel is not web: 401 unauthorized

x-endpoints.note: Fetched and cached by the gateway when it boots; the gateway also keeps identical built-in copies.

unknown_call.when: turn or end for a call_id the brain has never started

stale_timestamp.when: gateway timestamp more than 120 s from the brain's clock

unauthorized.when: no credentials, bad or expired bearer token, token for another call, channel not allowed for these credentials

rate_limited.when: web session limit reached (20 per hour per IP address)

invalid_request.when: body is not valid JSON or does not match the request schema; malformed call_id; unsupported lang

stale_seq.when: turn seq lower than the last accepted seq of the call

conflict.when: turn for a call that has already ended

locked.when: not used by the Brain API endpoints (shared code list)

not_found.when: not used by the Brain API endpoints (shared code list)

gone.when: not used by the Brain API endpoints (shared code list)

internal.when: unexpected brain failure; sending the same seq again is safe

start.brain_target: under 50 ms, never calls the language model

end.brain_target: under 50 ms, never calls the language model

lines_and_health.brain_target: under 50 ms, never calls the language model

turn_silence.brain_target: under 100 ms, never calls the language model

x-timing.budget_note: Gateway budgets are totals including at most one retry.
x-timing.retry: The gateway retries once, only after a connection error or a 502/503/504 status, and only with at least 2 s of the budget left. A retry sends the same request again (same seq).
failure_ladder: 1st consecutive failure: say GatewayLines.retry, then repeat the last ask
2nd consecutive failure: say GatewayLines.fatal, then hang up
failed start: say GatewayLines.fatal_start, then hang up
failed silence request: the client may answer it on its own by repeating the last ask; at the third silence in a row it says GatewayLines.no_input_bye and hangs up (end reason no_input)

phone_say_and_ask.numbers: in words: money as 'three hundred six dollars'; phone numbers and codes digit by digit in groups ('four one five, three three eight, one two zero three'); keypad keys as 'press one'
phone_say_and_ask.urls: spoken: 'gatorplate dot fly dot dev slash go'
phone_say_and_ask.markup: plain sentences only: no markdown, emoji or markup tags

never_in_any_reply: a rejection ('not eligible', 'ineligible', 'don't qualify', 'denied', 'no califica', 'no eres elegible')
a promise of a text message, a callback, a live transfer, a reminder message, or that anything was 'sent to the coordinator'
a claim of relay-service support or of 'any language'
an eligibility decision ('you qualify', 'you are eligible', 'approved'): only the county decides
x-text-rules.amounts: every estimated amount is followed in the same reply by the county-decides sentence

x-word-budgets.counted: words of say and ask together
x-word-budgets.word: a whitespace-separated token that contains at least one letter or digit ('student-built' and "isn't" are one word; a lone dash is none)

classes.result: a reply whose say gives an outcome or contact details to keep: the estimate or a routing result, the expedited outlook, the apply-today and card lines, or a phone number (coordinator, county, crisis)
classes.question: every other reply: acknowledgement plus the next question, confirmations, re-asks, short notices, goodbyes without a phone number

x-reply-rules: The /start reply has a non-empty say, a question in ask (the consent question), end false and interruptible false (the opening disclosure is never interruptible). On the phone, say states that GatorPlate is an AI, student-built and not an official SF State service, that an AI turns what the student says into text to check CalFresh, and that the call audio isn't recorded; ask asks for consent with the keypad option ('press one').
Phone replies: display, choices and card_url are always null; lang is en except a single-reply Spanish notice (language.offer_web).
Web replies: display is always a string; card_url, once set, stays set in every later reply of the call.
end true: the client says say and hangs up; ask is null, hold_s is 0, interruptible is false.
say empty, ask null and end false: the client says nothing and keeps listening (for example after a keypad key that is part of a longer entry).

hold_s 1-60: ask is null; the client keeps listening and sends no silence event for hold_s seconds. If the student is still silent when the hold ends, the client may say the last ask again; then silence events resume as usual.
choices only together with a question (ask not null).
debug is null unless the brain runs with GP_DEBUG_KEYS=1 (never in production).

Channel.description: phone = hosted voice gateway; web = GatorPlate talk page.

StartRequest.title: StartRequest
StartRequest.description: Body of POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/start. Sent once when the call begins. A repeated start returns the stored first reply. Unknown properties are ignored (tolerant reader).

channel.description: Must match the credentials: gateway signature = phone, bearer token = web.

lang.description: Phone: always en. Web: the language the student picked on the talk page.

test.description: true for a test call placed by the team, not by a student.

TurnRequest.title: TurnRequest
TurnRequest.description: Body of POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/turn. Exactly one event per request: utterance needs text, dtmf needs dtmf, silence needs silence_n. Fields that belong to another event are ignored. Unknown properties are ignored (tolerant reader).

seq.description: 1 for the first turn, then +1 per turn request. Same seq = same request (idempotent).

lang.description: Language of the text. Phone: always en. Web: the talk page's current language. Default: the call's language.

event.description: What happened: the student spoke or typed (utterance), pressed keypad keys (dtmf), or stayed silent (silence).

text.description: utterance: the final transcript (or typed text). No partial transcripts. May be empty; the brain then re-asks.

masked.description: utterance, phone: true when the gateway replaced a run of 9 or more digits (SSN, phone or card number) with '#' characters. The number of '#' characters carries no meaning.

confidence.description: utterance: how sure the transcript is, 0 to 1, or null when unknown.

interrupted.description: utterance: the student spoke over the previous reply.

typed.description: utterance: the text was typed, not spoken (web typing mode and quick replies; on the phone only in test calls). It does not mark a test call: only StartRequest.test does.

dtmf.description: dtmf: the keypad key pressed. The phone gateway sends every key press as its own dtmf event (exactly one key) and never collects several keys into one event; a brain that accepts a longer keypad entry (for example an amount ending with #) collects the keys itself and answers each key before the last with an empty reply. Up to 20 keys are accepted for tolerance.

silence_n.description: silence: how many silence events in a row, counting from 1. Any utterance or dtmf resets the count.

silence_ms.description: silence: approximate time since the student last spoke or pressed a key, in milliseconds; it grows with silence_n (informational only).

EndRequest.title: EndRequest
EndRequest.description: Body of POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/end. Sent once when the call is over, possibly before /start finished. Unknown properties are ignored (tolerant reader).

reason.description: completed / declined / no_input: the client ended the call after a reply with end true and that end_reason (no_input also when the gateway ends a silent call on its own). caller_hangup: the student hung up or left. timeout: replies did not arrive in time and the fatal line was said. max_duration: the call reached its time limit (the time_limit line was said). error: any other failure ended the call (including a failed /start). The brain treats timeout and error alike.

turns.description: Number of student turns sent in the call: utterance and dtmf requests, each seq counted once. Silence events are not counted.

EndResponse.title: EndResponse
EndResponse.description: Body returned by /end: an empty object.

ReplyEndReason.description: Why the brain ends the call (only with end true).

BrainReply.title: BrainReply
BrainReply.description: Reply to /start and /turn. Every property is always present. The client says say, then ask. All wording comes from GatorPlate's sentence bank; numbers are inserted by code.

say.description: Statement spoken first. May be empty (with ask null and end false: say nothing and keep listening). On /start: the opening disclosure, never empty. Phone replies stay far below the limit because of the word budgets; the limit leaves room for longer web replies in Spanish.

ask.description: The question, spoken after say, or null. Always interruptible. The gateway repeats the last non-null ask after the retry line.

end.description: true: say, then hang up (phone) or close the conversation (web).

lang.description: Language to speak this reply in. Phone: en, or es for a single Spanish notice. Web: the conversation language.

listen.description: normal, or long = patient end of turn and a longer silence timeout (amounts, slow talkers).

expect.description: Kind of answer the ask expects: open, yes_no, confirm (yes or no about a value just repeated back), number, choice.

interruptible.description: May the student cut off say? Always false for the /start reply and for end replies.

hold_s.description: 0, or 1-60 when the student asked to wait: keep listening and send no silence event for this many seconds. If the student is still silent when the hold ends, the client may say the last ask again; then silence events resume as usual.

display.description: Web only: on-screen text of this reply (say and ask together) with digits and symbols. Always null on the phone.

choices.description: Web only: quick-reply labels for the ask; a tap sends the label as an utterance with typed true. Null when there are none and always null on the phone.

card_url.description: Web only: same-origin path of the student's card once it exists, else null. Always null on the phone.

debug.description: Null unless GP_DEBUG_KEYS=1 (never in production): the sentence keys used for this reply and the conversation phase.

GatewayLines.title: GatewayLines
GatewayLines.description: Fixed lines the gateway says on its own (GET /v1/lines). All wording is owned by GatorPlate; the gateway caches them at boot and keeps identical built-in copies. Spoken text: same rules as phone replies.

filler.description: One is said when a turn reply (utterance or dtmf) has not arrived after 1.5 s.

retry.description: Said before repeating the last ask after the first consecutive failure.

fatal.description: Said after the second consecutive failure; then hang up.

fatal_start.description: Said when /start fails; includes the AI disclosure; then hang up.

no_input_bye.description: Said if the gateway ends a silent call on its own; then hang up.

time_limit.description: Said when the call reaches its time limit; then hang up (end reason max_duration).

line_unavailable.description: Said instead of a conversation when the phone line cannot take a call right now (for example, the team switched it off); then hang up.

WebSessionRequest.title: WebSessionRequest
WebSessionRequest.description: Body of POST /api/web/sessions (no auth, 20 per hour per IP address). May be empty ({}). Unknown properties are ignored.

lang.description: Language the student picked. Default en.

WebSessionResponse.title: WebSessionResponse
WebSessionResponse.description: A new web call: its call_id and a bearer token bound to it for 30 minutes.

token.description: Opaque URL-safe token with at least 128 bits of randomness.

ErrorCode.description: Machine-readable error code; HTTP status and retryable flag per code are listed in x-errors.

ErrorEnvelope.title: ErrorEnvelope
ErrorEnvelope.description: Body of every non-200 response. The message is short and generic: no stack traces, no request text.

retryable.description: true when sending the same request again later may succeed.
